builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks
summary: Replaces passive logging and generic traffic analysis with active honeypot probes that force agentic attackers to reveal model identity and harness behavior through resource-access constraints. Costs involve deploying and maintaining modular honeypot services and designing discriminative interaction traps that induce model declarations and characteristic outputs. Fails if attackers employ models or harnesses outside the trained classifier's coverage, if agents use strong obfuscation or non-standard harnesses not represented in the evaluation set, or if behavioral probes do not generalize to unseen task families.
rationale: Defenders operating honeypots or security telemetry can use these shibboleth traps to attribute agentic attacks to specific model versions and harnesses without requiring expensive infrastructure or large-scale training.

Costs involve deploying and maintaining modular honeypot services and designing discriminative interaction traps that induce model declarations and characteristic outputs. Fails if attackers employ models or harnesses outside the trained classifier's coverage, if agents use strong obfuscation or non-standard harnesses not represented in the evaluation set, or if behavioral probes do not generalize to unseen task families.
Distinguishes among 15 candidate models with an average 90% top-1 accuracy; identifies correct harness among four candidates with 92% accuracy using fixed probe rules.
